reasoning: A base plus a breakout, not a level. ITW fell 297.32 to a 263.99 close on 9 September, spent eleven sessions inside 265.14-270.79, then closed through that shelf at 273.42 on 1.68M shares and held 272.00 on a down day for SPY. From memory, with no precise figures, ITW is a decades-long dividend raiser with a conservative balance sheet, and that is a recollection, not an input. At about $272, 4 shares is roughly $1,088, or 8.2% of a ~$13,300 book, and $4,834 of cash covers it easily. It fills the tenth and last slot and is my first industrials name, so no sector goes over three.

Floor the position in the session it opens. $260.00 sits beneath the 261.35 intraday low of 10 September and beneath every close of the base (lowest 263.99). On a daily-close check it fires only if the whole 264-270 shelf is gone and the 297-to-264 decline has started again. That means the thesis is finished, not wobbling. It exits the whole position at about -4.4% instead of riding to the -15% stop near $231. It is one rung on all four shares, because a new position whose thesis is 'the shelf held' cannot be half wrong. I ladder it once it has earned a ladder.

Protective rail for the REP fill, which arrived at 31.54 on the 09/24 close, not at my 31.30 stop, so the level is anchored to what I actually paid. 29.55 sits 0.27% under 29.63, the 09/23 open that was also that bar's low. The one fresh headline (EU methane rules on crude supply, 09/24) is regulatory noise, not a crack-spread change, and the tape is the argument. Sized 70 to match the position exactly.

Risk is -9.69% from the close. Median bar on this leg is 5.30% (4.90, 3.94, 6.97, 5.30, 7.80, 5.59, 2.05), so the stop is 1.83x that and clears my 1.4x floor. Tighter levels don't pass: under the 248.51 low of 9/23 is -4.3%, only 0.81x. The line moves from -2.29% to -0.37% against my 235.38 entry, close to breakeven on a +10% winner.

The rule forces this one; my test didn't invite it, and I'll say so plainly. ILMN made a higher low at 250.92 against 247.00, but the bar widened from 3.59% to 9.87%, so the test fails. Against the normal bars of this leg (8.48, 5.37, 5.62, 5.69, 4.21, 3.59, median 5.50%, leaving out tonight's 9.87% outlier) that is 1.80x, clear of my 1.4x floor. The line moves from -8.96% to -3.38% against my 255.38 entry.

Gap-and-flag breakout: the 9/21 +11.3% gap was never filled, the flag made three higher lows, and 9/24 broke out +4.50% to a one-year closing high of 777.59 at 94% of range on 1.56x volume while SPY and QQQ were flat. This ratchets the Agilent rail from 152.00 to 156.90 USD, replacing ord_2026-09-24_world_003, which I cancel in the same session. It is sized to exactly the nine shares I hold. The structure advanced 4.55% in one session and the level did not: 152.00 now sits 12.1% beneath a 172.84 close, which is protection nobody would call a rail. Placement is structural. The closes of the breakout leg run 153.69, 156.34, 156.47, 161.94, 165.32 and 172.84, so 156.90 sits in the untraded closing gap between the 156.47 of 09-18 and the 161.94 of 09-21. A fire means the whole post-shelf advance has failed back into the launch base, and that falsifies the sector re-rating. At -9.22% from 172.84 the rail is 3.4 daily ranges away on a 2.68% mover, just outside the 3.0 I default to. That is deliberate after a +4.55% day, when the next session's give-back is ordinary. The move takes protection from -8.06% on cost to -5.09%, about 76 USD or 67 EUR of risk. The date stays 10-15 with the rest of the book. FX stance: the rail is written in dollars, and on a day EURUSD made a fresh low at 1.1382 the currency leg is working for me, not against me.

This is a retest entry on Sartorius Stedim at 206.00 EUR: six shares, about 1,236 EUR and 12.3% of a 10,045 EUR book, against my 20% cap. It would be the sixth position of twelve, funded from 2,901 EUR of cash. Asset thesis: bioprocessing and life-science tools are re-rating together. On 09-24 DIM.PA, SRT3.DE and A each rose more than 4.5%, and DHR and WAT printed sixty-day closing highs on volume. The euro end of that is Sartorius Stedim, which cleared the whole 203-208 September ceiling (highs of 203.0 and 208.0, closes of 205.6 and 206.4) and closed on its 215.80 high. I will not buy the top of a five-percent candle eight sessions and 17% off a low. That is the Altria mistake. 206.00 is the broken ceiling itself, the 205.6-206.4 closing band of 09-22/23 and just above the 205.0 low of the breakout bar. A fill there is the market proving old resistance is now support. At -4.5% from the close it is 1.7 daily ranges on a 2.7% mover, a normal retest rather than a hope. If it fills, the rail goes beneath the 198.1 close of 09-18 in the next session. It expires 10-09, because a breakout that never retests in two weeks has left without me, and that is acceptable. Tools would total about 26% of book with A, in line with the airline pair at 28%. That is the ceiling for this theme, not a start. FX stance: euro-quoted, no currency leg, and deliberately so. It adds euro weight to a book whose sterling leg is drifting against me, and it expresses the same sector view as Agilent without doubling my dollar.
